answer: Persistent route fingerprinting. Each agent must publish a signed activity trail through fixed infrastructure nodes, and its identity key is derived from the unique traversal history of those nodes. A duplicate agent replaying the same trail is detected as a falcon circling identical ground, since no two honest agents share a route. Copying another's history forces the attacker to physically re-walk every karst relay and pay each node's toll, making each forged identity cost the full voyage of real traversal rather than a cheap key copy.
